support.note: NVIDIA only (CUDA, g++ and the CUDA toolkit to build). README: RTX 20 or newer; sm_60 (Tesla P100) is covered by the Pascal-compat fork. Not yet: AMD cards.

notes: PolyStrata (github.com/festeraeb/PolyStrata, fork of VecSzn/PolyStrata). `polystrata-serve` is a one-line wrapper on lemond's PATH: exec python3 <PolyStrata>/serve/server.py "$@" (see docs/POLYSTRATA.md).
{model} is the run config JSON that PolyStrata's setup writes (strata-<name>.json: exe, args, tokenizer, model_name, GGUF path), not the GGUF itself. {device} is the nvidia-smi index (PCI bus order).

GAP (checked 2026-10-31, d52354d6; confirmed through lemond 2026-11-10 with the Nauti-Strata build of the same server): PolyStrata's /v1/models objects have no `owned_by` field and lemond refuses the load when the spec names one, so identity.unreported is set here (the plane skips the check) until PolyStrata adds "owned_by": "polystrata" to them. Lemonade also already lists a running PolyStrata as a cloud provider (docs/LEMONADE.md) without this adapter.
/health answers only once the engine is up ({"status":"ok","loaded":true,"service":"strata"}), after the first start's compile and expert-cache fill.
LFM2.5-24B-A2B (LiquidAI LFM Open License v1.0, not open source) runs in it as the `lfm25` family; GPU: 8 GB or more.
Not tested through this adapter. The CUDA cards were not on a node when it was written. No NautiBurn scrape hook: the scraper rule is open for this engine.
